claims.claim: Caveolins associate with cavin family proteins (cavins 1–4) to stabilize caveolae at the plasma membrane.
claims.source: Caveolins associate with cavin family proteins (cavins 1–4) to stabilize caveolae at the plasma membrane.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about caveolae structure.

claims.claim: Cavin 1 is essential for caveolae formation in mammalian cells.
claims.source: Cavin 1 (also known as Polymerase I and transcript release factor PTRF) is essential for caveolae formation in mammalian cells (Hill et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2008) by interacting with Cav1 (in non-muscle cells) and Cav3 (in muscle cells).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Cavin 1 interacts with Cav1 in non-muscle cells and Cav3 in muscle cells.
claims.source: Cavin 1 (also known as Polymerase I and transcript release factor PTRF) is essential for caveolae formation in mammalian cells (Hill et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2008) by interacting with Cav1 (in non-muscle cells) and Cav3 (in muscle cells).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Cavin 4 is not required for caveolae formation but may play a role in caveolar morphology.
claims.source: The muscle-specific cavin 4 isoform (also known as muscle-restricted coiled-coil, MURC), the last described caveolae protein (Ogata et al., 2008), is not required for caveolae formation but may play a role in caveolar morphology (Bastiani et al., 2009; Lo et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: In skeletal muscle, Cav3 localizes mostly on the plasma membrane of mature fibers but is also present at the core of the fiber where it is associated with the T-tubule system.
claims.source: In skeletal muscle, Cav3 localizes mostly on the plasma membrane of mature fibers but is also present at the core of the fiber where it is associated with the T-tubule system (Ralston and Ploug, 1999).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Plasma membrane openings of caveolae and T-tubules are of the same size (20–40 nm) and appear indistinguishable by electron microscopy.
claims.source: Plasma membrane openings of caveolae and T-tubules are of the same size (20–40 nm) and appear indistinguishable by electron microscopy (EM) (Franzini-Armstron, 1974; Franzini-armstrong and Porter, 1964).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous EM studies.

claims.claim: Caveolae are enriched at the neck of T-tubules at the plasma membrane.
claims.source: This similarity between caveolae and T-tubules (Ishikawa, 1968), as well as their dependence on membrane cholesterol (Hidalgo et al., 1986; Rothberg et al., 1992; Yuan et al., 1991), the enrichment of caveolae at the neck of T-tubules at the plasma membrane (Franzini-Armstrong, 1991; Murphy et al., 2009), and the association of Cav3 with developing T-tubules (Parton et al., 1997) all suggest that caveolae and their associated proteins could have a role in T-tubule biogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Cav3 is associated with developing T-tubules.
claims.source: This similarity between caveolae and T-tubules (Ishikawa, 1968), as well as their dependence on membrane cholesterol (Hidalgo et al., 1986; Rothberg et al., 1992; Yuan et al., 1991), the enrichment of caveolae at the neck of T-tubules at the plasma membrane (Franzini-Armstrong, 1991; Murphy et al., 2009), and the association of Cav3 with developing T-tubules (Parton et al., 1997) all suggest that caveolae and their associated proteins could have a role in T-tubule biogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Caveolae may fuse together and form a substrate for proteins capable of tubulating membranes such as Bin1.
claims.source: It has been suggested that caveolae may fuse together and form a substrate for proteins capable of tubulating membranes such as Bin1 (also known as amphiphysin 2) (Lee et al., 2002) and more recently, a direct interaction between Bin1 and cavin 4 was shown to be required for normal T-tubule formation in zebrafish muscle (Lo et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: A direct interaction between Bin1 and cavin 4 is required for normal T-tubule formation in zebrafish muscle.
claims.source: It has been suggested that caveolae may fuse together and form a substrate for proteins capable of tubulating membranes such as Bin1 (also known as amphiphysin 2) (Lee et al., 2002) and more recently, a direct interaction between Bin1 and cavin 4 was shown to be required for normal T-tubule formation in zebrafish muscle (Lo et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a recent study.

claims.claim: Mutations in the CAV3 gene cause autosomal dominant neuromuscular diseases called caveolinopathies.
claims.source: The importance of these proteins in skeletal muscle physiology is emphasized by the fact that mutations in the CAV3 gene cause autosomal dominant neuromuscular diseases called caveolinopathies (Aboumousa et al., 2008; Gazzerro et al., 2010; Woodman et al., 2004) and mutations in BIN1 induce T-tubule and triad defects in the autosomal recessive form of centronuclear myopathy (Nicot et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Mutations in BIN1 induce T-tubule and triad defects in the autosomal recessive form of centronuclear myopathy.
claims.source: The importance of these proteins in skeletal muscle physiology is emphasized by the fact that mutations in the CAV3 gene cause autosomal dominant neuromuscular diseases called caveolinopathies (Aboumousa et al., 2008; Gazzerro et al., 2010; Woodman et al., 2004) and mutations in BIN1 induce T-tubule and triad defects in the autosomal recessive form of centronuclear myopathy (Nicot et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claims.claim: Bin1 splicing defects in the exon responsible for the interaction of Bin1 with membrane phosphoinositides induce T-tubule defects in myotonic dystrophy.
claims.source: In addition, Bin1 splicing defects in the exon responsible for the interaction of Bin1 with membrane phosphoinositides induce T-tubule defects in myotonic dystrophy (Fugier et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: In patients with caveolae deficiency and in Cav3 knock-out mice, defects in T-tubule orientation and defects in calcium flow are observed.
claims.source: In patients with caveolae deficiency and in Cav3 knock-out mice, defects in T-tubule orientation and defects in calcium flow are observed, although T-tubules still develop (Galbiati et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: T-tubules still develop in patients with caveolae deficiency and in Cav3 knock-out mice.
claims.source: In patients with caveolae deficiency and in Cav3 knock-out mice, defects in T-tubule orientation and defects in calcium flow are observed, although T-tubules still develop (Galbiati et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Nascent T-tubules initially have a longitudinal orientation during in vitro differentiation.
claims.source: Nascent T-tubules initially have a longitudinal orientation during in vitro differentiation, and progressively gain a transversal orientation reflecting extensive differentiation (Flucher et al., 1993; Takekura et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Nascent T-tubules progressively gain a transversal orientation reflecting extensive differentiation.
claims.source: Nascent T-tubules initially have a longitudinal orientation during in vitro differentiation, and progressively gain a transversal orientation reflecting extensive differentiation (Flucher et al., 1993; Takekura et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Tagging Cav3 with GFP produced a very characteristic pattern on unroofed myotubes with numerous circular or crescent-shaped structures from which tubules emanated.
claims.source: At the light microscopy level, tagging Cav3 with GFP produced a very characteristic pattern on unroofed myotubes with numerous circular or crescent-shaped structures from which tubules emanated (Figure 1A, insets 1–5).
claims.evidence: This is a primary observation supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: The diameter of Cav3 rings from human myotubes expressing Cav3GFP was 652±174 nm.
claims.source: The diameter of these rings from either human myotubes expressing Cav3GFP or murine myotubes labeled with antibodies against Cav3 was the same, 652±174 nm and 637±183 nm, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claims.claim: The diameter of Cav3 rings from murine myotubes labeled with antibodies against Cav3 was 637±183 nm.
claims.source: The diameter of these rings from either human myotubes expressing Cav3GFP or murine myotubes labeled with antibodies against Cav3 was the same, 652±174 nm and 637±183 nm, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claims.claim: RyR1-labeled structures were often surrounded by or in close proximity to Cav3 rings.
claims.source: RyR1-labeled structures were often surrounded by or in close proximity to Cav3 rings (insets in Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is an observation supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: Circular assemblies composed of bona fide caveolae were confirmed in human myotubes at the ultrastructural level.
claims.source: At the ultrastructural level, in addition to the numerous individual caveolae decorating the cytoplasmic side of the plasma membrane, we confirmed the presence of circular assemblies composed of bona fide caveolae in human myotubes (Figure 1C–E).
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding supported by EM data shown in Figure 1C-E.

claims.claim: Caveolae rings were composed of assembled caveolae forming a circle.
claims.source: These 'caveolae rings' were composed of assembled caveolae forming a circle.
claims.evidence: This is a description of the observed structure.

claims.claim: The central part of the caveolae ring contained globular membrane proteins.
claims.source: The central part of the ring contained globular membrane proteins (Figure 1C–E, orange circles).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from EM data shown in Figure 1C-E.

claims.claim: Similar caveolae rings were observed in mouse primary myotubes using both PREM and conventional thin-section EM.
claims.source: We observed similar caveolae rings in mouse primary myotubes using both PREM and conventional thin-section EM (Figure 1, F-G).
claims.evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 1F-G.

claims.claim: The average diameter for caveolae rings was 573 nm in human myotubes and 546 nm in murine primary myotubes.
claims.source: From measurements on electron micrographs, we determined an average diameter for these rings of 573 nm in human myotubes and 546 nm in murine primary myotubes (Figure 1H).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from EM data shown in Figure 1H.

claims.claim: There were 16.9 caveolae per ring on average in human myotubes and 16.1 in mouse myotubes.
claims.source: We counted 16.9 and 16.1 caveolae per ring on average in human and mouse myotubes respectively (Figure 1I).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from EM data shown in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: Caveolae from primary mouse myotubes were significantly smaller than their human counterparts (64 vs 85.4 nm).
claims.source: Caveolae from primary mouse myotubes were significantly smaller than their human counterparts (64 vs 85.4 nm, respectively) (Figure 1J).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from EM data shown in Figure 1J.

claims.claim: The circular Cav3 assemblies seen at the light microscopy level correspond to rings formed by caveolae.
claims.source: Using this CLEM approach, we were able to show that the circular Cav3 assemblies seen at the light microscopy level correspond to rings formed by caveolae (Figure 1, K-M).
claims.evidence: This is supported by CLEM data shown in Figure 1K-M.

claims.claim: Caveolae rings were found in proximity with the cortical endo/sarcoplasmic reticulum.
claims.source: While analyzing caveolae rings by CLEM, we observed a proximity with the cortical endo/sarcoplasmic reticulum (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from CLEM data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The cortical ER/SR either contacted the center or was entangled with the caveolae ring.
claims.source: We found numerous instances where the cortical ER/SR either contacted the center or was entangled with the caveolae ring (Figure 2B–C).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from EM data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claims.claim: Direct SR-caveolae contacts were never observed.
claims.source: We never observed direct SR-caveolae contacts but rather an interaction between the SR and regions of the ring devoid of caveolae, confirming our previous observations using super-resolution (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from EM data.

claims.claim: The α1s-subunit of the DHPR accumulated in regions of the plasma membrane enriched in Cav3-positive circular caveolae regions from which tubules appear.
claims.source: CLEM analysis confirmed that the α1s-subunit of the DHPR accumulated in regions of the plasma membrane enriched in Cav3-positive circular caveolae regions from which tubules appear.
claims.evidence: This is supported by CLEM data shown in Figure 2.

claims.claim: Both DHPR and Cav3 co-localized on nascent tubules, but the labeling was only present on portions of the tubule containing the caveolae.
claims.source: It is noteworthy that while both DHPR and Cav3 co-localized on nascent tubules, the labeling was only present on portions of the tubule containing the caveolae, suggesting a possible retention of the Ca2+ channel in caveolar regions (Figure 2H).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from CLEM data shown in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: Tubules with a characteristic beaded protein coat similar to the caveolar coat emerged from caveolae rings.
claims.source: By unroofing the myotubes, we noticed that tubules with a characteristic beaded protein coat similar to the caveolar coat emerged from caveolae rings (Figure 3A–C).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from PREM data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claims.claim: EM analysis of ultrathin sections from the adherent surface of myotubes confirmed the presence of bona fide caveolae rings from which numerous 25 nm diameter tubules emanated.
claims.source: EM analysis of ultrathin sections from the adherent surface of myotubes confirmed the presence of bona fide caveolae rings from which numerous 25 nm diameter tubules emanated (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by EM data shown in Figure 3D and supplement.

claims.claim: Endogenous Cav3 and Bin1 are present on caveolae rings and on the tubules emanating from these rings.
claims.source: Using our CLEM approach, we showed that endogenous Cav3 and Bin1 are present on caveolae rings but also on the tubules emanating from these rings (Figure 3E–H and I–L, Figure 3—video 1 and Figure 3—video 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by CLEM data shown in Figure 3E-L.

claims.claim: Numerous Cav3-positive rings could be resolved on the myotube surface during live imaging.
claims.source: Numerous Cav3-positive rings could be resolved on the myotube surface.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from live imaging experiments.

claims.claim: Live imaging captured numerous tubules emanating from rings and could measure tubule extension.
claims.source: Our imaging captured numerous tubules emanating from rings and could measure tubule extension (Figure 4A and Figure 4—video 1, Figure 4—video 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4A and videos.

claims.claim: Cav3GFP-labeled structures moved at 45.7±22 nm/s.
claims.source: Analysis of their dynamics showed Cav3GFP-labeled structures moving at 45.7±22 nm/s.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from live imaging data.

claims.claim: Bright Cav3 spots appeared before the tubule at the same site where the tubule emanated.
claims.source: Interestingly, bright Cav3 spots appeared before the tubule at the same site where the tubule emanated (yellow arrows in Figure 4A, B) suggesting that Cav3 polarized accumulation observed by PREM (Figure 1D, E) could precede tubulation.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from live imaging data shown in Figure 4A-B.

claims.claim: Bin1 labeled structures move at 64.2±18 nm/s on average.
claims.source: Analysis of their dynamics showed that Bin1 labeled structures move at 64.2±18 nm/s on average.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from live imaging data.

claims.claim: While both Bin1-Δex11GFP and Bin1GFP-induced formation of caveolae rings with similar diameters and at the same density, only Bin1GFP-induced formation of tubules emanating from the rings.
claims.source: We transduced human myotubes for 24 hr and showed that while both Bin1-Δex11GFP and Bin1GFP-induced formation of caveolae rings with similar diameters and at the same density, only Bin1GFP-induced formation of tubules emanating from the rings (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 supplement 1.

claims.claim: Bin1GFP formed circular structures at the surface of myotubes that were also visible on unroofed myotubes.
claims.source: Bin1GFP formed circular structures at the surface of myotubes that were also visible on unroofed myotubes (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from microscopy data shown in Figure 5A and supplement.

claims.claim: Cav3 co-localized with Bin1 on rings and at the base of Bin1 tubules.
claims.source: Immunofluorescent labeling with antibodies against endogenous Cav3 confirmed that these rings were also present on intact myotubes (Figure 5B) and that Cav3 co-localized with Bin1 on rings and at the base of Bin1 tubules.
claims.evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: While all the rings were positive for Bin1, Cav3 labeled only a subset suggesting that Bin1 acts upstream of Cav3.
claims.source: Interestingly, while all the rings were positive for Bin1, Cav3 labeled only a subset suggesting that Bin1 acts upstream of Cav3 (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B, with inference about the relationship.

claims.claim: Bin1 expression induced the formation of numerous beaded tubular structures that emanated radially from rings.
claims.source: Bin1 expression induced the formation of numerous beaded tubular structures that emanated radially from rings (Figure 5C, D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by PREM data shown in Figure 5C-D.

claims.claim: At 1 μM, recombinant Bin1 assembled into circular structures from which tubules emerged radially on supported lipid bilayers.
claims.source: Along this line, we observed that at 1 μM, recombinant Bin1 assembled into circular structures from which tubules emerged radially.
claims.evidence: This is supported by in vitro experiments with recombinant protein.

claims.claim: Recombinant Bin1 structures on lipid bilayers resembled those formed on the surface of cultured myotubes indicating that Bin1 is able to spontaneously form these scaffolds on flat membranes both in vitro and in cellulo.
claims.source: These structures, firmly bound to the lipid bilayer, resembled those formed on the surface of cultured myotubes indicating that Bin1 is able to spontaneously form these scaffolds on flat membranes both in vitro and in cellulo.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of in vitro and in cellulo data.

claims.claim: Bin1 forms stable ring-like structures and tubules that persist over several minutes on supported lipid bilayers.
claims.source: We showed that Bin1 forms stable ring-like structures and tubules that persist over several minutes (Figure 5G and kymographs in Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by time-lapse imaging data shown in Figure 5G and supplement.

claims.claim: Bin1 overexpression produced both pearled tubes with caveolar material and assemblies that were similar as those observed on SLBs with recombinant Bin1.
claims.source: Importantly, we observed that Bin1 overexpression produced both pearled tubes with caveolar material and assemblies that were similar as those observed on SLBs with recombinant Bin1 (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from microscopy data shown in Figure 5H.

claims.claim: The average diameter of Bin1 assemblies in vitro was 378±176 nm and in cellulo was 746±223 nm.
claims.source: The average diameter of Bin1 assemblies in vitro and in cellulo was 378±176 nm and 746±223 nm, respectively.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claims.claim: The average length of the longest tube emanating from the central ring was 1356 nm in vitro and 2200 nm in cellulo.
claims.source: The average length of the longest tube emanating from the central ring was 1356 nm in vitro and 2200 nm in cellulo while the average length of the smaller tubules emanating from the central ring was 420 nm in vitro and 590 nm in cellulo (Figure 5I).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 5I.

claims.claim: The average length of the smaller tubules emanating from the central ring was 420 nm in vitro and 590 nm in cellulo.
claims.source: The average length of the longest tube emanating from the central ring was 1356 nm in vitro and 2200 nm in cellulo while the average length of the smaller tubules emanating from the central ring was 420 nm in vitro and 590 nm in cellulo (Figure 5I).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data shown in Figure 5I.

claims.claim: Bin1 overexpression induced formation of pearled tubes with the same caveolar coat.
claims.source: Bin1 overexpression in human myotubes induced formation of pearled tubes with the same caveolar coat (Figure 6A and inset in 3D anaglyph).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from PREM data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Bin1 labeled tubules formed in regions enriched with caveolae.
claims.source: CLEM analysis with Bin1GFP allowed us to show that Bin1 labeled tubules formed in regions enriched with caveolae (Figure 6B, D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by CLEM data shown in Figure 6B and D.

claims.claim: The fluorescence corresponding to Bin1 localization was not always associated with caveolae rings at the ultrastructural level.
claims.source: We observed that the formation of tubular and circular structures of the plasma membrane perfectly correlating with Bin1 fluorescence. However, the fluorescence corresponding to Bin1 localization was not always associated with caveolae rings at the ultrastructural level (Figure 6E, G).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from CLEM data shown in Figure 6E and G.

claims.claim: Bin1 could self-assemble into platforms which act as scaffolds for recruitment of caveolae.
claims.source: These circular structures, which resemble caveolae rings, suggested that Bin1 could self-assemble into platforms which act as scaffolds for recruitment of caveolae.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of Bin1 structures without caveolae.

claims.claim: Bin1 overexpression lead to the formation of numerous Cav3-positive rings from which pearled tubules emerged in primary mouse myotubes.
claims.source: We confirmed these observations by transducing primary mouse myotubes (Figure 6H, K and Figure 6—video 1). Bin1 overexpression lead to the formation of numerous Cav3-positive rings from which pearled tubules emerged (Figure 6I, K).
claims.evidence: This is supported by CLEM data shown in Figure 6H-K.

claims.claim: Intact myotubes expressing Bin1 presented a circular organization of 25–40 nm openings characteristic of caveolae necks seen from outside.
claims.source: While extremely rare in control myotubes, intact myotubes expressing Bin1 presented a circular organization of 25–40 nm openings characteristic of caveolae necks seen from outside (Figure 7A, B).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from PREM data shown in Figure 7A-B.

claims.claim: The membrane invaginations labeled by the MemBright probe co-localized with Bin1 labeling demonstrating that the tubules formed by Bin1 are in continuity with the extracellular medium.
claims.source: The membrane invaginations labeled by the probe co-localized with Bin1 labeling demonstrating that the tubules formed by Bin1 are in continuity with the extracellular medium.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the MemBright penetration assay data.

claims.claim: Rings were labelled with both MemBright and Bin1GFP.
claims.source: In agreement with our previous observations, we detected rings that were labelled with both MemBright and Bin1GFP (Figure 7D).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the MemBright assay shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: Cav3 knock-down resulted in a significant decrease in both the tubulation of membranes formed by Bin1 and the total Bin1 fluorescence.
claims.source: The 2 siRNAs used enabled a 65–85% decrease in total Cav3 protein leve (Figure 7F, G) and resulted in a significant decrease in both the tubulation of membranes formed by Bin1 and the total Bin1 fluorescence (Figure 7E and H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by siRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7E-H.

claims.claim: Cav3-depleted myotubes formed small Bin1-positive foci at the plasma membrane without extending into tubes.
claims.source: In contrast to controls, Cav3-depleted myotubes formed small Bin1-positive foci at the plasma membrane without extending into tubes confirming the importance of Cav3 structures as initiators of Bin1-induced tubule formation.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from siRNA knockdown experiments.

claims.claim: The decrease in Cav3 protein levels in differentiated patient myotubes was confirmed using Western blotting.
claims.source: The decrease in Cav3 protein levels in differentiated patient myotubes was confirmed using Western blotting (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 8 supplement 1.

claims.claim: Patient myotubes were still capable of forming caveolae at the sarcolemma as observed by high-resolution PREM.
claims.source: While we observed a drastic reduction in the amount of Cav3 at the plasma membrane (Gazzerro et al., 2010), myotubes were still capable of forming caveolae at the sarcolemma as observed by high-resolution PREM (Figure 8A–C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from PREM data shown in Figure 8A-C and supplement.

claims.claim: A Western-blot screen between control and R26Q patient myotubes showed no difference in Bin1 and Junctophilin 2 expression levels, RyR1 and DHPRα1s subunit.
claims.source: A Western-blot screen between control and R26Q patient myotubes showed no difference in Bin1 and Junctophilin 2 (SR protein forming contacts between terminal cisternae and T-tubules) expression levels. (Takeshima et al., 2000), RyR1 and DHPRα1s subunit (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 8 supplement 1.

claims.claim: Caveolae in patient myotubes displayed an altered structure and spatial organization.
claims.source: Ultrastructural analysis showed that the spatial organization of caveolae in ring-like structures was altered. We observed instances of deformed rings with supernumerary caveolae (Figure 8A).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from PREM data shown in Figure 8A.

claims.claim: A unique feature of patient myotubes was the production of beaded tubes composed of 5–10 concatenated caveolae not associated with a ring.
claims.source: A unique feature of patient myotubes was the production of beaded tubes composed of 5–10 concatenated caveolae not associated with a ring (Figure 8C and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from PREM data shown in Figure 8C and supplement.

claims.claim: R26Q patient myotubes showed significantly less caveolae rings at the surface compared to control myotubes.
claims.source: Quantification of caveolae rings from R26Q patient myotubes showed significantly less caveolae rings at the surface of patient myotubes (in agreement with a decreased Cav3 surface expression) and an increase in their average diameter compared to control myotubes (Figure 8F and G).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from microscopy data shown in Figure 8F-G.

claims.claim: R26Q patient myotubes showed an increase in caveolae ring average diameter compared to control myotubes.
claims.source: Quantification of caveolae rings from R26Q patient myotubes showed significantly less caveolae rings at the surface of patient myotubes (in agreement with a decreased Cav3 surface expression) and an increase in their average diameter compared to control myotubes (Figure 8F and G).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from microscopy data shown in Figure 8F-G.

claims.claim: Cav3 re-expression rescued caveolae ring density while reducing the average diameter to control values.
claims.source: Cav3 re-expression rescued caveolae ring density while reducing the average diameter to control values.
claims.evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments with Cav3 re-expression.

claims.claim: Myotubes from R26Q patients transduced with Bin1GFP showed a significant decrease in tubule density compared to cells from controls.
claims.source: Myotubes from R26Q patients were transduced with an adenovirus expressing Bin1GFP vector for 24 hr that resulted in a significant decrease in tubule density compared to cells from controls (Figure 8H–J).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8H-J.

claims.claim: Analysis of skeletal muscle biopsies using thin-section EM tomograms showed characteristic but rare triad abnormalities including T-tubule bifurcations and swelling of the T-tubules.
claims.source: Analysis of skeletal muscle biopsies using thin-section EM tomograms showed characteristic but rare triad abnormalities including T-tubule bifurcations (Figure 8K–M and Figure 8—video 1) and swelling of the T-tubules (Figure 8N).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from EM data of patient biopsies shown in Figure 8K-N.

claims.claim: Clustered caveolae are present at the T-tubule initiation site.
claims.source: Pioneer work on early T-tubule formation in muscle has shown that clustered caveolae are present at the T-tubule initiation site (Franzini-Armstrong, 1991; Ishikawa, 1968; Parton et al., 1997; Schiaffino et al., 1977) and that both structures present similar lipid composition, that is enriched in cholesterol and sphingolipids (Parton et al., 1997).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Caveolae and T-tubules present similar lipid composition, enriched in cholesterol and sphingolipids.
claims.source: Pioneer work on early T-tubule formation in muscle has shown that clustered caveolae are present at the T-tubule initiation site (Franzini-Armstrong, 1991; Ishikawa, 1968; Parton et al., 1997; Schiaffino et al., 1977) and that both structures present similar lipid composition, that is enriched in cholesterol and sphingolipids (Parton et al., 1997).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Caveolae assemble into higher order, 600 nm on average, ring-like structures in mouse and human muscle cells.
claims.source: Our discovery that caveolae assemble into higher order, 600 nm on average, ring-like structures in mouse and human muscle cells suggests that caveolae may be involved in the formation of membrane platforms on the surface of muscle cells that could participate in T-tubule biogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claims.claim: Overexpressing Bin1 induced formation of a dense network of membrane tubules.
claims.source: In agreement with previous reports, overexpressing Bin1 induced formation of a dense network of membrane tubules (Nicot et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is supported by experimental data and citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Cav3 knock-down lead to a drastic reduction of Bin1-induced tubes.

results.result: Caveolae assemble into ring-like structures (~600 nm diameter) composed of 16-17 individual caveolae in both human and mouse myotubes, as demonstrated by super-resolution microscopy, PREM, and CLEM.
results.evaluation: Multiple complementary imaging techniques (super-resolution microscopy, PREM, thin-section EM, and CLEM) consistently demonstrate circular caveolae assemblies with quantified diameters and caveolae counts. The CLEM approach directly correlates fluorescent Cav3 signals with ultrastructural caveolae rings, providing strong convergent evidence.

results.result: Caveolae rings are spatially associated with cortical SR/ER cisternae containing RyR1, with the SR contacting regions of the ring devoid of caveolae rather than the caveolae themselves.
results.evaluation: CLEM and EM data consistently show proximity and entanglement between caveolae rings and RyR1-positive SR membranes, with specific observation that SR contacts ring regions lacking caveolae. This spatial relationship is well-documented across multiple imaging modalities.

results.result: The DHPR α1s-subunit accumulates in Cav3-positive caveolae ring regions and co-localizes with Cav3 on nascent tubules, with labeling restricted to caveolae-containing portions of tubules.
results.evaluation: CLEM analysis with GFP-tagged DHPR α1s-subunit demonstrates co-localization with Cav3 on rings and tubules. The observation that DHPR/Cav3 labeling is restricted to caveolae-containing tubule regions is supported by correlative imaging data.

results.result: Tubules with beaded caveolar coats emanate from caveolae rings, and both endogenous Cav3 and Bin1 are present on these rings and emanating tubules.
results.evaluation: PREM, thin-section EM, and CLEM consistently demonstrate tubules with caveolar coats emerging from rings. Double-labeling CLEM experiments confirm co-localization of endogenous Cav3 and Bin1 on both rings and tubules, providing strong structural and molecular evidence.

results.result: Live imaging reveals dynamic tubule extension from Cav3-positive rings, with Cav3-labeled structures moving at 45.7±22 nm/s and Bin1-labeled structures at 64.2±18 nm/s, with Cav3 accumulation preceding tubulation.
results.evaluation: Time-lapse imaging provides direct visualization of tubule dynamics with quantified velocities. The observation of Cav3 spot appearance before tubule emergence is documented in sequential frames, though the temporal relationship could benefit from higher temporal resolution.

results.result: Bin1 overexpression induces formation of both rings and tubules, with the muscle-specific isoform (including exon 11) required for tubulation but not ring formation, and Bin1 acting upstream of Cav3 recruitment.
results.evaluation: Comparative experiments with Bin1+exon11 vs Bin1-Δexon11 demonstrate differential effects on tubulation while maintaining similar ring formation. Immunofluorescence showing all rings positive for Bin1 but only a subset positive for Cav3 supports the upstream role, though the mechanistic basis requires further investigation.

results.result: Recombinant Bin1 spontaneously assembles into ring-like structures with emanating tubules on supported lipid bilayers containing PI4,5P2, resembling structures formed in cells and demonstrating Bin1's intrinsic scaffolding capacity.
results.evaluation: In vitro reconstitution experiments with recombinant Bin1 on defined lipid bilayers demonstrate spontaneous formation of rings and tubules with quantified dimensions. The structural similarity to cellular structures supports the model of Bin1 as a scaffold, though in vitro structures are smaller (378±176 nm vs 746±223 nm in cells).

results.result: Bin1 overexpression in myotubes produces pearled tubules with caveolar coats in caveolae-enriched regions, but Bin1 fluorescence is not always associated with caveolae rings at the ultrastructural level.
results.evaluation: CLEM analysis demonstrates Bin1-labeled tubules in caveolae-enriched regions with characteristic beaded morphology. The observation of Bin1 structures without associated caveolae rings suggests Bin1 can form scaffolds independently, supporting the proposed recruitment model.

results.result: Bin1-induced tubules are continuous with the extracellular space, as demonstrated by circular organization of 25-40 nm caveolae neck openings visible from outside and MemBright probe penetration.
results.evaluation: PREM imaging from the extracellular side shows organized caveolae openings, and the MemBright penetration assay provides functional evidence of continuity with extracellular space. Co-localization of MemBright with Bin1GFP on rings confirms the structures are open invaginations.

results.result: Cav3 knockdown by siRNA results in 65-85% reduction in Cav3 protein and causes significant decrease in Bin1-induced tubulation and total Bin1 fluorescence, with formation of small Bin1-positive foci instead of extended tubes.
results.evaluation: Western blot confirms substantial Cav3 depletion, and quantitative imaging demonstrates significant reduction in both tubulation and Bin1 fluorescence. The phenotypic change from tubes to foci provides strong evidence for Cav3's requirement in Bin1-mediated tubulation.

results.result: Patient myotubes with CAV3 mutations (P28L, R26Q) show reduced Cav3 at the plasma membrane but retain some caveolae with altered ultrastructure, including deformed rings, beaded tubes of concatenated caveolae, and significantly fewer rings with increased diameter.
results.evaluation: Western blot confirms reduced Cav3 levels in patient cells, and PREM reveals specific ultrastructural abnormalities. Quantification shows significant differences in ring density and diameter. The presence of some caveolae despite reduced Cav3 suggests partial compensation, possibly by Cav1.

results.result: Cav3 re-expression in patient myotubes rescues caveolae ring density and diameter to control values, while patient myotubes transduced with Bin1GFP show significantly decreased tubule density compared to controls.
results.evaluation: Rescue experiments demonstrate that Cav3 re-expression reverses the patient phenotype, establishing causality. The reduced Bin1-induced tubulation in patient cells provides functional evidence linking Cav3 deficiency to impaired membrane tubulation.

results.result: Skeletal muscle biopsies from caveolinopathy patients show rare but characteristic triad abnormalities including T-tubule bifurcations and swelling.
results.evaluation: EM tomography of patient biopsies documents specific T-tubule abnormalities. However, the claim that these are 'rare' suggests limited penetrance or sampling issues. The structural defects are consistent with the proposed role of Cav3 in T-tubule formation.

results.result: SR-T-tubule junctions form on smooth tubule regions devoid of caveolar material, and the caveolar coat disappears as tubules protrude deeper into the cytoplasm, suggesting caveolar protein disassembly is required for functional junction formation.
results.evaluation: EM observations consistently show junctions forming on caveolae-free tubule regions and progressive loss of caveolar coat with tubule depth. The proposed mechanism of caveolar protein removal is supported by structural evidence and agreement with zebrafish studies, though direct evidence of disassembly is lacking.

results.result: Caveolae rings (~600 nm diameter) represent essential structures for T-tubule initiation, potentially serving as the missing link in understanding T-tubule biogenesis.
results.evaluation: The discovery of caveolae rings is well-supported by multiple imaging modalities. Their consistent size, composition, and association with nascent tubules support their role in T-tubule formation. However, the claim of being 'essential' and the 'missing link' represents interpretation beyond the direct experimental evidence.

results.result: The proposed model suggests Bin1 forms circular scaffolds that recruit Cav3-positive caveolae, which merge and accumulate at ring poles, with the muscle-specific Bin1 isoform enabling tubule extension from multiple positions on the ring.
results.evaluation: This mechanistic model integrates multiple observations but contains substantial speculation. While Bin1 scaffold formation and caveolae recruitment are supported by data, the specific mechanisms of caveolae fusion, polarized accumulation, and the role of lipid enrichment lack direct experimental evidence. The model is plausible but requires validation.

results.result: Cavin 4 directly interacts with Bin1 and may play a role in T-tubule membrane remodeling by recycling caveolae, with cavin 4 deletion resulting in pearled tubule formation.
results.evaluation: These claims are primarily based on cited literature (Lo et al., 2021) rather than data presented in this manuscript. The cited work provides evidence for the Bin1-cavin 4 interaction and its role in T-tubule formation, which is appropriately referenced.

results.result: The mixed wild-type and mutant Cav3 population in patient caveolae may prevent DHPR enrichment and reduce Bin1 tubulation, with patient myotubes showing reduced Ca2+ release/influx and DHPR-RyR1 colocalization defects.
results.evaluation: The proposed mechanism for how mutant Cav3 affects DHPR enrichment and Bin1 tubulation is speculative. While patient cells show functional defects (Ca2+ handling, DHPR-RyR1 colocalization) supported by citations, the mechanistic link to the mixed Cav3 population is hypothetical and requires direct testing.

results.result: Nascent T-tubules initially have longitudinal orientation during in vitro differentiation and progressively gain transversal orientation reflecting extensive differentiation.
results.evaluation: This is established knowledge supported by appropriate citations (Flucher et al., 1993; Takekura et al., 2001) and confirmed by the authors' observations in Figure 1 supplement showing the progression from longitudinal to transverse organization.

results.result: Prior work has established that caveolae participate in T-tubule formation, are enriched at T-tubule necks, associate with developing T-tubules, and share similar lipid composition with T-tubules.
results.evaluation: These claims accurately represent established knowledge from the cited literature. The authors appropriately contextualize their work within the existing framework of caveolae involvement in T-tubule biogenesis.

results.result: Mutations in CAV3 cause caveolinopathies and mutations in BIN1 cause centronuclear myopathy, with patients showing T-tubule defects, Cav3 aggregation at the Golgi, and symptoms including myalgias and exercise intolerance.
results.evaluation: These claims accurately represent established clinical and molecular knowledge supported by appropriate citations. The pathological consequences of CAV3 and BIN1 mutations are well-documented in the literature.
